newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Comalco sees early Boyne smelter start.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Comalco sees early Boyne smelter start.

text.p: Expansion work at Queensland's Boyne Island aluminium smelter is running several months ahead of schedule, which should allow production to start around June 1997, a spokesman for Comalco Ltd said on Monday.
Installation of a third potline at the smelter will lift annual capacity by 217,000 tonnes to around 480,000 tonnes, the spokesman said.
Comalco owns 50 percent of the existing Boyne Island smelter and will hold a 59.25 percent interest in the third potline.
Production from the third potline will be progressively built up to operate at full capacity, the spokesman said.
Comalco had earlier said it expected the third potline to start up sometime in the third quarter of calendar 1997.
Comalco last week said its Bell Bay aluminium smelter in Tasmania state would reach full capacity in early September, producing about 119,000 tonnes in 1996.

The Bell Bay smelter had been operating about 28,000 tonnes a year below capacity since February 1994 when Comalco shut down one of three potlines at the plant as part of an international production cutting arrangement to reduce a global supply overhang.
The arrangement expired earlier this year.
